criteria.criterion: When a session reference is configured, an eBay search fetch request carries it.
criteria.plannedImplementation: Add a nullable SessionReference to ScrapeClientOptions and ScrapeJobRequest, then have HttpScrapeClient.StartJob build the api/NewJob request with _options.SessionReference so the configured value is serialized into the outgoing request body alongside the search url.
criteria.plannedVerification: SessionReferenceCarriedOnSearchFetchTests.Should_carry_the_configured_session_reference_on_the_new_job_request constructs an HttpScrapeClient with ScrapeClientOptions whose SessionReference is 'operator-session-token', runs GetPageHtml against a capturing HttpMessageHandler, parses the captured api/NewJob body and asserts the session-reference property equals the configured value. At base StartJob still builds ScrapeJobRequest([url]) so the captured body has a null reference and the assertion fails on the missing behaviour. No existing check inspects the NewJob request body; EbaySearchUrlServiceTests only covers url construction.
materialConcerns: wire compatibility with the external scraper: the NewJob body must carry the reference in a field the scraper accepts
the session reference is credential-like and must not be written to logs

criteria.criterion: When no session reference is configured, the fetch request carries none and behaves as today.
criteria.plannedImplementation: Leave SessionReference null when the Scraper:SessionReference configuration value is absent and omit a null session reference from the serialized NewJob body, so an unconfigured fetch keeps the current urls-only request.
criteria.plannedVerification: FetchRequestWithoutSessionReferenceTests.Should_omit_the_session_reference_when_none_is_configured constructs an HttpScrapeClient with SessionReference unset, captures the api/NewJob body and asserts it contains no session-reference property while still containing the search url. At base the null property is serialized as "SessionReference":null, so the absence assertion fails while the url assertion shows the request is otherwise unchanged. No existing check inspects the NewJob body.
materialConcerns: public-contract compatibility: callers that do not configure a session reference must see the same request as today
the anonymous NewJob body must keep working against the scraper without a session field

criteria.criterion: The session reference is read from configuration, not hard-coded.
criteria.plannedImplementation: Read Scraper:SessionReference in ServiceCollectionExtensions.BuildScrapeClientOptions and pass it into the registered ScrapeClientOptions so the HTTP client receives the operator-configured value rather than a literal.
criteria.plannedVerification: SessionReferenceFromConfigurationTests resolves ScrapeClientOptions from AddCoreServices(configuration): Should_read_the_session_reference_from_configuration asserts Scraper:SessionReference='configured-session' reaches options.SessionReference; Should_change_the_resolved_session_reference_when_configuration_changes asserts two different configured values resolve to their own values; Should_leave_the_session_reference_unset_when_configuration_does_not_provide_it asserts the value is null or empty when the key is absent. At base BuildScrapeClientOptions never reads Scraper:SessionReference, so the first two fail. The existing ScraperClientConfigurationTests covers only Scraper:BaseUrl and Scraper:ApiKey.
materialConcerns: secret handling: a session reference is sensitive and must come from configuration rather than source
the configuration key must sit in the existing Scraper section so operators configure it the same way as BaseUrl and ApiKey

comparisonObservation.firstObservation: the first configuration value resolves to its own session reference, e.g. 'first-session' in configuration produces options.SessionReference 'first-session'
comparisonObservation.whenHeldValueAbsent: when no Scraper:SessionReference value is held, options.SessionReference is null or empty rather than a hard-coded literal
